honest.pitch: A Chrome extension that drafts Reddit replies for community managers at small SaaS companies, so they stop spending evenings writing the same answers by hand

candidate.headline: Policy-Safe Answers for High-Stakes Reddit Questions
candidate.short_description: Retrieve current, approved Reddit answer cards for sensitive SaaS questions, or escalate when no defensible response exists.
candidate.description: ReplyMatch is a Chrome extension and lightweight approval ledger for the moment a SaaS operator is about to answer a Reddit question about pricing, security, integrations, outages, roadmap commitments, eligibility, or regulated/compliance-sensitive claims. Rather than trying to automate every Reddit reply or compete with bundled inboxes, it retrieves a versioned, owner-approved answer card only when the visible thread satisfies a narrow policy/topic match. Each card carries source links, product/version scope, required qualifiers, an expiry/review date, and an accountable approver. If the match is weak, stale, contradicted by thread context, or outside policy, ReplyMatch blocks one-click reuse and creates a compact approval request with the exact question and deadline. The operator can paste a cited, on-brand response in seconds, or route the exception before an inaccurate public commitment is made.
candidate.value_proposition: Help small SaaS teams respond quickly to high-stakes Reddit questions with the current, approved product answer—and force an escalation when no defensible answer exists—instead of offering another generic social inbox or AI reply writer.
core_features: Reddit composer detection that extracts the question, parent context, subreddit, and optional highlighted text without requiring a Reddit publishing API
Versioned approved-answer cards for high-risk SaaS topics: pricing/plan limits, security and privacy, integrations, uptime/incidents, support boundaries, roadmap language, and eligibility
Conservative match gate combining topic classifiers, semantic similarity, product/version tags, required-context checks, and freshness thresholds; no one-click answer below threshold
Mandatory-answer constraints: approved wording, required caveats, prohibited claims, canonical evidence links, card owner, and expiry/re-certification date
Context conflict detection that flags mismatched plan, region, product version, or claim and routes to review rather than reusing a superficially similar reply
One-click paste of a short approved response plus optional public documentation link; no autonomous posting
Slack/email/webhook escalation packet containing the Reddit permalink, extracted context, proposed card, missing facts, approver, and response-SLA countdown
Audit trail showing what was pasted, which approved card/version supported it, who approved exceptions, and which cards are expiring or repeatedly requested
Request analytics that identify unanswered public objections and obsolete documentation, not vanity inbox metrics
candidate.why_it_works: The modal operational risk is not that every Reddit question repeats verbatim; it is that questions recur as variable phrasings around a small set of consequential claims. Topic and scope routing can reliably identify these classes even when exact-answer retrieval cannot. For high-confidence, current matches, a pre-approved answer eliminates search and copy-editing delay. For the larger ambiguous tail, the product does not pretend retrieval is enough: it captures the complete context, enforces a response deadline, and sends the decision to the accountable owner. This directly uses the urgency in faster, on-brand, compliant, error-free replies while avoiding commoditized inbox, reporting, and generic AI-drafting capabilities.
candidate.innovation_angle: The wedge is not reply management or generic retrieval. It is a browser-native 'claim safety gate' for public Reddit responses: approved knowledge is treated as expiring, scoped policy evidence, and uncertainty is an explicit workflow outcome. ReplyMatch wins only on the risky long-tail questions where a fast but unverified answer can create a pricing promise, security misstatement, roadmap commitment, or compliance problem.
differentiation_factors: Unlike generic social inboxes, it activates only for narrow high-stakes Reddit questions rather than attempting to manage every channel and interaction.
Unlike AI reply writers, it retrieves versioned, owner-approved answer cards and blocks unsupported reuse instead of generating an unaccountable claim.
The differentiation lives at the pre-posting decision point: thread-aware policy matching, expiry checks, contradiction detection, and mandatory escalation.
A lightweight Chrome extension and approval ledger fit small SaaS teams that need governance without adopting a full social media suite.
candidate.differentiation_locus: The browser-extension interception of the Reddit composer, combined with a team-owned knowledge base of expiring, scoped approved answers that forces escalation when no defensible answer exists. Rivals like KWatch.io and F5Bot monitor Reddit but don't integrate into the response workflow; broad suit
candidate.technical_approach: Build a Manifest V3 extension with a Reddit-specific content script and a local extraction layer for composer text, parent/comment-tree context, permalink, subreddit, and explicit user selection. Send minimized context to a tenant backend. Model approved cards as structured records with claim class, product/plan/version/region scope, answer text, mandatory qualifiers, forbidden language, citations, owner, approval state, and expiry. Use deterministic eligibility filters first (scope, freshness, required entities and exclusions), then embeddings plus a lightweight reranker to propose candidates. A calibrated confidence policy permits paste only when the best card clears semantic, scope, and freshness thresholds and no conflict detector fires. Otherwise, generate an escalation request rather than a draft. Store immutable event records and card versions. Integrate with a team's existing Slack/email and documentation system; initial ingestion is manual CSV/Notion/help-center import with explicit approval, avoiding dependence on social-platform APIs. Security controls include tenant isolation, encryption, role-based card approvals, short retention for captured thread context, and user-visible confirmation before any text is pasted.
target_personas: Small SaaS community manager handling repetitive product questions
SaaS founder or support lead responsible for maintaining approved public answers
candidate.data_acquisition_notes: The extension reads the publicly visible Reddit thread and explicitly selected composer context through the browser page; no Reddit API or bulk scraping is required. Customers supply the approved answer cards, citations, scope, and approval metadata, so the core route is public page context plus tenant-provided data with no external licensing cost.
